prose: Troy Hunt's weekly update dwells on the gap between breach perception and reality, especially the newsroom narrative of AI as the big bad hacking tool. The counter-evidence he collects: AI has had literally 0% impact on insurance payouts for cyber incidents; a Dutch suspect is being tracked down based on his voice; and a much-discussed MAG breach teardown by Scott ultimately traced back to exposed keys rather than anything sophisticated.

His favorite example of the distortion: an Australian headline claiming ChatGPT had hacked a court system, when in fact someone had simply used ChatGPT to write a scraper and pointed it at the court's website. The mundane truth, Hunt notes, just doesn't make for good headlines.
highlights: AI-as-hacking-tool hype: 0% impact on cyber insurance payouts so far
Dutch suspect tracked down by his voice
MAG breach teardown pointed to exposed keys, not sophisticated attack
The 'ChatGPT hacked a court system' story was really a ChatGPT-written scraper
Hunt's moral: the truth doesn't make for good headlines
